minutes.headline: Select Board voted 4-0 to support the water district's pilot study to treat the Hickory Hills well.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was a Lunenburg Water District and Tighe & Bond presentation on reactivating the Hickory Hills well, with Hickory Hills lake residents raising concerns about the lake. The board also heard the school committee's sidewalk request and busing update, ratified a heavy equipment operator, reviewed warrant articles, the 300th anniversary charge, and donation bins, then went into executive session.

public_comment.topic: A board member reported on the donation boxes at the Walmart parking lot and her contact with Standard Recycling, who will install cameras.
Announcement of a pancake breakfast and the start of the ZBA 40B Pond View Commons hearing.
Concerns about the lake, the shallow well and the small zone around it; urged looking at other well sites.
Easement disagreement, impact of moving a treatment plant, and how the study and any new well would be paid for.
Water commissioner supported the pilot to get ahead of PFAS rules and funding.
Suggested a fallback water interconnection, as with Fitchburg.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-0 to support the water district's plan for a pilot study of the Hickory Hills well.
Most of the meeting was the water district's presentation on reactivating the well; lake residents raised concerns about the lake, the shallow well and the easement.
The district said the pilot would be paid from its system enhancement fund of connection fees, with later treatment through state loans and rates, not a betterment.
The board voted unanimously to authorize the town manager to file an asset management grant application with MassDEP.
The board ratified a heavy equipment operator appointment; the 300th anniversary charge and a letter to Brixmore on donation bins return for a vote next week.

why_it_matters: The Hickory Hills well pilot is the first step toward a possible treatment plant, and the minutes say later treatment would be paid through state loans and water rates rather than a betterment, so it may reach water bills.
The pilot is funded from connection fees rather than the town budget, but a full treatment plant was described as a larger cost the district is not pursuing now.
watch_next: The Select Board's vote on the revised 300th anniversary committee charge, expected next week.
The town manager's draft letter to Brixmore about litter and the donation bins, due for the board next week.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. reconciliation.summary: The records agree on all three votes and most figures, with remaining differences mostly caption misspellings of names and amounts. The main thing to know is that our minutes carry several decisions and figures (Brixmore letter, hybrid ZBA hearings, site visits, Keating well cost, and goals display) that the official minutes do not record; the goals display is the one conflict, since the official minutes record only a suggestion.
